answer: Registration binds each identity to a 300-unit bond held against one hardware attestation key, recorded once per device in a public registry called the trellis. A sybil attacker locking N identities pays 300N units upfront, and any proven duplicate forfeits the full bond plus a 30-epoch freeze on re-registration. Splitting a device across fake keys adds 300 units marginal cost per identity, while independent jurors flag cloned keys and slash the shared bond under the velvet audit rule and the quill log.
